# N9: The flagship goal page: five journeys at 390 and 1280; status once, no repeats, what to act on in the first screen, motion and Share

A check of the core ([the journeys](../journeys.md)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/9-goal-page.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured.

## What it checks

the flagship goal page (approved by Lane, 5 Nov). Five journeys from the plan, each at 390 and 1280: J1 a leader scans an off-track north star (Lead time for changes, as Amara); J3 an owner answers a review question from Home without scrolling; J5 an owner posts a check-in and sees it land; J6 drilling into the goal most likely to make it miss, and back to the parent by name; J8 a first-time viewer from a shared key link, then coming back. And the page's promises: the goal's status once in the first screen, no reason repeated, Next steps and asks within the first phone screen and Why before the chart (GT1, Lane 10 Nov; it was the chart before), nothing moving under reduced motion (and nothing over 250ms otherwise), Share producing an image and a link. The scorecard (Lane, 5 Nov, on a phone: "the target four times, the trend three times"): under the status and the number, four labelled cells (vs plan, vs last week, to target, will it hit), the target said once in the first screen, the same numbers marked on the chart, nothing restated under it; the reason opening Why, the feeds heading What feeds it; every section headed and saying what it answers; the one-line bar a solid panel that stands off the page.

## What it reports as wrong

- {at6}: Back did not return to the north star
